research_rationale: EO 799 (signed 1908-05-23 by Theodore Roosevelt, held ProQuest scan text) excuses from duty, for the parade in connection with the removal of the body of Vice-President Clinton on May 27, 1908, the listed patriotic-society members employed in the District of Columbia in the executive departments and independent establishments. The Register and WPA entry for 1908 May 23 p.92 agree with the text on date and subject. The order is a single one-time permission with one clause and no later-reaching command. It is spent by its own terms on the stated day: May 27, 1908 is recorded inclusive (the excusal covers that whole day), the exclusive reading being that it ends when that day begins. Held searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, OFR catalog) found no hit for this order, and the corpus search for the number found only the Wikisource neighbour-navigation pages of EO 798 and EO 800, which are not later events affecting it.
savings_reason: The order grants only an excusal from duty on one day for one parade; nothing in its text creates a continuing right, transfer or obligation. No held source records any consequence that survives May 27, 1908.
earlier_end_check: The order's only date is May 27, 1908; no earlier revocation, supersession or recall appears in the held corpus search for the number (hits only the navigation pages of EO 798 and EO 800) or in the OFR, U.S. Code and eCFR machine searches (0 hits).
scope_check: The single paragraph is the whole order: it names the societies, the class of employees, the parade of May 27, 1908 and the excusal. There is no other operative clause.
independent_command_check: There is no independent command: the only operative words excuse the named employees from duty for the parade.
savings_check: The excusal was an exhausted one-day permission; no savings or residual effect is shown in any held source.

research_rationale: EO 1087 (signed 1909-06-15 by William H. Taft; held Wikisource revision 1766830) permits Miss Hattie M. Miller to be reinstated in the Patent Office as a classified laborer at $600 without regard to the length of time since her separation. The Register and WPA entry (1909 June 15 p.115, 1909 CSR 131) agree on person, grade and date. The held Wikisource text of EO 1093 (signed 1909-06-21) authorizes reinstating the same person in the same office as a skilled laborer and carries the editorial annotation "Superseded Executive Order 1087, June 15, 1909."; the held page of EO 1087 carries the matching annotation. The end is recorded as supersession by EO 1093 on 1909-06-21. Disclosure: the supersession word appears in the transcription's annotation, not in EO 1093's own operative sentence, which grants a replacement reinstatement of the same person; no held source shows whether a reinstatement under EO 1087 was actually made before 1093. The name-match lead EO 4131 (ProQuest scan) is an unrelated order on Alaska military reservations and does not mention this order or this person. Machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, OFR catalog) found no hits for EO 1087.
savings_reason: EO 1087 is a one-person permission to reinstate; its operative effect was replaced by EO 1093 for the same person and office. No held source shows any surviving command, and any personnel action taken under it would be a completed act, not a continuing order.
earlier_end_check: No instrument earlier than EO 1093 (1909-06-21) affecting EO 1087 appears: the corpus search for the number finds only the EO 1086 navigation page and the EO 1093 annotation, and the machine searches have 0 hits.
scope_check: The single sentence is the whole order; its one clause is the permission to reinstate Miss Hattie M. Miller as a classified laborer. EO 1093 replaces it for the same person and office.
independent_command_check: No independent command: the order only permits one reinstatement without regard to length of separation.
savings_check: The permission was replaced by EO 1093; no continuing effect of EO 1087 is shown in any held source.
